title: Enterprise Dedicated Intake: SLA & Burst-resiliency Sizing Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a practical, repeatable playbook and intake form for enterprise Dedicated capacity requests that balances SLA targets, reserved throughput sizing, GPU class recommendations, and burst/graceful-degradation policies. This will standardize onboarding, reduce sizing rework, and provide clear guidance to sales/solutions on what to commit to in a contract.
background: Multiple recent enterprise wins required multiple hand-offs between Solutions, Sales, and Eng to agree reserved throughput SLAs and burst behavior. We lost time sizing GPU class and scaling policies because intake signals were inconsistent. Existing intake templates surface peak RPS but not token distributions or acceptable degradation modes. This causes conservative over-provisioning and delayed onboarding.
goal: Ship a v1 playbook and updated intake questionnaire + a reference GPU-sizing matrix and SLA template that reduces initial sizing variance by 50% and shortens time-to-provision by 30% for typical enterprise requests.
acceptance_criteria: [1] A completed intake form template that collects workload shape (qps, tokens per request distribution, tail percentiles), acceptable SLOs (p95 latency, max queueing delay), and degradation modes. [2] GPU-sizing matrix (A100-40/T4 etc) with guidance by model family, sequence length, and concurrency. [3] Standardized SLA language and burst policies for contracts. [4] Playbook published in Confluence with a linked checklist used in 3 pilot onboardings.
sizing_guidance_summary: Recommend GPU class by workload buckets: conversational short-turn (<=256 tokens): prefer lower-cost GPU with strong fp16 kernels; long-context generation (>1024 tokens) and high throughput: recommend A100-80 or H100 equivalent. For mixed workloads use tiering with small fast nodes for low-latency requests and cheap batch nodes for background inference.
burst_policy_principles: 1) Defined burst window (30s / 1min) with limited reserved burst tokens. 2) Graceful degradation: degrade non-critical routes, reduce max_response_tokens, enable KV-prefix cache for cold starts. 3) Hard quota fallback: synthetic 429 with informative header for callers. 4) Auto-fallback to lower-cost model variant if latency SLOs would be violated.
intake_form_highlights: Collect: workload archetype, 95/99 token length percentiles, expected steady-state qps, expected burst factor, acceptable latency SLOs, customer must-protect routes, regional constraints, security/compliance notes, preferred GPU families, cost sensitivity and whether deterministic outputs required.
playbook_steps: 1) Intake submission and automatic pre-check that flags missing signals. 2) Quick sizing runbook (est. 2 days): baseline throughput calc, token/sec estimate, recommended GPU pool. 3) Eng review and optional load test plan. 4) Canary provisioning + 72h telemetry review. 5) Finalize SLA and commit.
decision_log: 2025-02-20: Agreed to include 'acceptable degradation modes' as mandatory intake field after solutions feedback. 2025-02-24: Chose to recommend model-variant fallbacks in playbook rather than enforcing single global fallback due to customer diversity. 2025-02-28: Opted for two-tier burst windows (30s fast, 5min extended) to align with existing autoscaler behavior.
tradeoffs: Mandating more fields increases intake friction for sales and could slow initial contact; mitigated with a short 'quick intake' and follow-up deep intake. Conservative GPU recommendations reduce risk but increase cost—we provide a delta-cost estimate for customers to choose a lower-cost staging pool.
pilot_plan: Select three incoming enterprise requests across finance, healthcare, and commerce. Run playbook end-to-end with solutions + eng. Collect provisioning time, rework count, and SLA breaches over first 14 days. Iterate on intake fields based on pilot feedback.
metrics_to_track: time_to_first_provisioning, provisioning_rework_count, p95_latency_post_provision, tokens_per_second_observed, cost_per_1M_tokens, burst_eviction_rate
rollout_plan: Week 1: publish playbook + intake form. Week 2-5: pilot with 3 customers. Week 6: iterate and publish v1.1. Week 8: bake into onboarding checklist and update Sales/SE templates.
onboarding_checklist: 1) Intake complete, 2) Pre-sizing calc attached, 3) Eng review scheduled, 4) Load test plan attached or waived, 5) Canary window scheduled, 6) SLA doc drafted, 7) Billing/commit guidance shared.
risks: Under-collection of token distribution data may force conservative sizing. Customers may request unsupported GPUs in remote regions. Legal may require specific SLA phrasing that conflicts with technical fallbacks.
mitigations: Add mandatory example payloads to intake, provide region availability matrix, loop in Legal early on SLA draft step.
implementation_notes: Create a small HTTP-based pre-checker that validates intake payload and returns missing fields. Add an internal 'sizing calculator' spreadsheet and embed in Confluence. Runtime to provide a recommended model-variant mapping API (PR exists).
qa_steps: 1) Review with Eng and Solutions. 2) Test intake pre-checker against 10 anonymized past requests. 3) Validate GPU recommendations against internal perf bench. 4) Run a simulated burst test on staging clusters.
